title: In de stad
subtitle: Places and opening hours
intro: In this lesson you learn to name useful places in town, such as the bakery, the pharmacy and the library. You also learn to ask about opening hours and to say where you are going with gaan + naar.

example.nl: Het centrum is in de stad.
example.en: The centre is in the town.

words.note: You already know de stad from u01-l04; here it contrasts with het centrum.

example.en: I am going to the town centre.
Where is the station?
The library is open today.
The town hall is closed.
I am going to the pharmacy.

example.nl: De bakker is van acht tot zes open.
example.en: The bakery is open from eight to six.

words.note: De bakker can mean the shop or the person.

example.en: I have to go to the butcher.
The drugstore is closed today.
The post office is closed.
The bank is open tomorrow.

words.note: Also means couch, as in u04-l01.

example.nl: Het park is in het centrum.
example.en: The park is in the centre.
The museum is open today.
I am going to the cinema.
The hospital is big.
The shop is open.
The bank is closed today.
The library is closed.

words.note: More formal than dicht; common on signs.

example.nl: De openingstijden zijn van negen tot vijf.
example.en: The opening hours are from nine to five.

example.nl: De winkel is open tot vijf uur.
example.en: The shop is open until five o'clock.

example.nl: Vanaf maandag is de bank open.
example.en: From Monday the bank is open.

example.nl: De apotheek is van negen tot vijf open.
example.en: The pharmacy is open from nine to five.
I am going to the station.

words.note: Use naar for movement to a place.

grammar.title: naar, in of bij?
grammar.explanation: Use **naar** for movement to a place: **Ik ga naar de bakker.** Use **in** for inside a place: **Ik ben in de bibliotheek.** Use **bij** for at a shop, a counter or someone's place: **Ik ben bij de bakker.**

examples.en: I am going to the bakery.

grammar.tip: Think: naar = moving, in = inside, bij = at the shop or counter.

grammar.title: Openingstijden: van ... tot ...
grammar.explanation: Ask **Hoe laat gaat ... open?** or **Hoe laat gaat ... dicht?** Answer with **van ... tot ...**: **De winkel is van negen tot vijf open.** **Vanaf** means from a starting point: **Vanaf maandag is de bank open.**

rows: Hoe laat gaat de bakker open?
De bakker gaat om acht uur open.
Hoe laat gaat de bank dicht?
De bank gaat om vijf uur dicht.

examples.nl: De apotheek is van negen tot vijf open.
examples.en: The pharmacy is open from nine to five.

examples.nl: Vanaf maandag is de bank open.
examples.en: From Monday the bank is open.

grammar.tip: Use **om** before a clock time: om negen uur.

grammar.title: Gaan + naar: Ik ga naar de bibliotheek.
grammar.explanation: **Gaan** means to go. Use **naar** before the place. The forms are **ik ga**, **jij gaat**, **wij gaan**. In a question with jij, the -t drops: **Ga jij naar de bank?**

examples.en: I am going to the library.
Are you going to the bakery?

grammar.tip: Put the place after **naar**: naar de bakker, naar het station.

dialogue.title: Op zaterdag in de stad
dialogue.setting: It is Saturday. Sanne and Mark are in the town centre. They need bread, a book and a few errands.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Ik ga naar de bakker. Ik moet brood halen.
lines.en: I am going to the bakery. I need to fetch bread.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.nl: Hoe laat gaat de bakker open?
lines.en: What time does the bakery open?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Om acht uur. De bakker is van acht tot zes open.
lines.en: At eight o'clock. The bakery is open from eight to six.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.nl: En de apotheek? Is de apotheek open?
lines.en: And the pharmacy? Is the pharmacy open?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Ja, de apotheek gaat om negen uur open. Ik ga om tien uur naar de apotheek.
lines.en: Yes, the pharmacy opens at nine. I am going to the pharmacy at ten.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.nl: Ik ga naar de bibliotheek. Ik wil een boek kopen.
lines.en: I am going to the library. I want to buy a book.

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.nl: Ja, maar de openingstijden zijn anders. Van tien tot vier.
lines.en: Yes, but the opening hours are different. From ten to four.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: En de bank? Is de bank open?
lines.en: And the bank? Is the bank open?

lines.speaker: Mark
lines.nl: Nee, de bank is vandaag gesloten. De bank is morgen open.
lines.en: No, the bank is closed today. The bank is open tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Goed. Tot straks bij de bakker!
lines.en: Good. See you later at the bakery!

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'bij' instead of 'naar' for movement: 'Ik ga bij de apotheek.'
mistakes.explain: Use **naar** for moving to a place. Say 'Ik ga naar de apotheek.' **bij** means at the shop, e.g. 'Ik ben bij de apotheek.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'in' instead of 'naar' for movement: 'Ik ga in de apotheek.'
mistakes.explain: **in** means inside a place. For going there, use 'Ik ga naar de apotheek.'

mistakes.pattern: Omits article 'de' before apotheek: 'Ik ga naar apotheek.'
mistakes.explain: Apotheek is a de-word; use 'de apotheek': 'Ik ga naar de apotheek.'

mistakes.pattern: Wrong verb form 'gaat' with ik: 'Ik gaat naar de apotheek.'
mistakes.explain: With **ik**, gaan is 'ga': 'Ik ga naar de apotheek.'

exercises.en: The bakery is open from eight to six.
answers: De bakker is van acht tot zes open.
De bakker is open van acht tot zes.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'voor' instead of 'van' for the start time: 'De bakker is open voor acht tot zes.'
mistakes.explain: Use **van ... tot ...** for opening hours: 'De bakker is open van acht tot zes.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'om' before the end time: 'De bakker is open van acht om zes.'
mistakes.explain: Use **tot** for the end: 'van acht tot zes'. **om** is only for a clock time by itself: 'om acht uur'.

mistakes.pattern: Says the bakery is closed instead of open: 'De bakker is van acht tot zes gesloten.'
mistakes.explain: The English says open, so use **open**, not **gesloten** or **dicht**.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'naar' for being at the shop: 'Ik ben naar de bakker.'
mistakes.explain: Use **bij** for being at a shop: 'Ik ben bij de bakker.' **naar** is for movement: 'Ik ga naar de bakker.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'in' for at the shop: 'Ik ben in de bakker.'
mistakes.explain: **in de bakker** sounds like inside the baker. Say 'Ik ben bij de bakker.'

mistakes.pattern: Omits article 'de': 'Ik ben bij bakker.'
mistakes.explain: Use 'de bakker': 'Ik ben bij de bakker.'

mistakes.pattern: Wrong verb form 'is' with ik: 'Ik is bij de bakker.'
mistakes.explain: With **ik**, zijn is 'ben': 'Ik ben bij de bakker.'

mistakes.pattern: Gives a bare order without graag/alstublieft: 'Ik wil brood.'
mistakes.explain: Add **graag** or **alstublieft** to sound polite: 'Ik wil graag een brood.' / 'Mag ik een brood, alstublieft?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses informal 'alsjeblieft' to the baker after 'u': 'Mag ik een brood, alsjeblieft?'
mistakes.explain: The baker says **u**, so use **alstublieft**: 'Mag ik een brood, alstublieft?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses wrong verb form 'wilt' with ik: 'Ik wilt graag een brood.'
mistakes.explain: With **ik**, willen is 'wil': 'Ik wil graag een brood.'

mistakes.pattern: Places 'graag' after the noun at the end: 'Ik wil een brood graag.'
mistakes.explain: Put **graag** before the thing you want: 'Ik wil graag een brood.'

exercises.context: You are at the library. You want to know the opening time.
exercises.task: Ask what time the library opens.
examples: Hoe laat gaat de bibliotheek open?
Hoe laat is de bibliotheek open?

mistakes.pattern: Wrong word order in question: 'Hoe laat de bibliotheek gaat open?'
mistakes.explain: In a question the verb comes before the subject: 'Hoe laat gaat de bibliotheek open?'

mistakes.pattern: Omits 'open': 'Hoe laat gaat de bibliotheek?'
mistakes.explain: Add **open**: 'Hoe laat gaat de bibliotheek open?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'hoeveel' instead of 'hoe laat': 'Hoeveel laat gaat de bibliotheek open?'
mistakes.explain: Use **hoe laat** for time: 'Hoe laat gaat de bibliotheek open?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses two verbs: 'Hoe laat is gaat de bibliotheek open?'
mistakes.explain: Use either **gaat ... open** or **is ... open**: 'Hoe laat gaat de bibliotheek open?' / 'Hoe laat is de bibliotheek open?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'bij' for movement to the shops: 'Ik ga bij de bakker.'
mistakes.explain: Use **naar** for movement: 'Ik ga naar de bakker.' **bij** is for being at the shop: 'Ik ben bij de bakker.'

mistakes.pattern: Wrong verb form with ik: 'Ik gaat naar de bakker.'

say.en: The bakery is open. The pharmacy opens at nine.

turns.task: Ask what time the library opens.

Hoe laat is de bibliotheek open?

mistakes.pattern: Wrong word order in question: 'Hoe laat de bibliotheek gaat open?'
mistakes.explain: In a question the verb comes before the subject: 'Hoe laat gaat de bibliotheek open?'

mistakes.pattern: Omits 'open': 'Hoe laat gaat de bibliotheek?'
mistakes.explain: Add **open**: 'Hoe laat gaat de bibliotheek open?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'hoeveel' instead of 'hoe laat': 'Hoeveel laat gaat de bibliotheek open?'
mistakes.explain: Use **hoe laat** for time: 'Hoe laat gaat de bibliotheek open?'

say.nl: De bibliotheek is van tien tot vier open.

turns.task: Say that you are going to the library at eleven o'clock.

Om elf uur ga ik naar de bibliotheek.

mistakes.pattern: Starts with time but keeps subject before verb: 'Om elf uur ik ga naar de bibliotheek.'
mistakes.explain: After **om elf uur**, the verb comes second: 'Om elf uur ga ik naar de bibliotheek.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'op' for a clock time: 'Ik ga op elf uur naar de bibliotheek.'
mistakes.explain: Use **om** with clock times: 'om elf uur'.

mistakes.pattern: Omits article 'de' before bibliotheek: 'Ik ga om elf uur naar bibliotheek.'
mistakes.explain: Use 'de bibliotheek': 'Ik ga om elf uur naar de bibliotheek.'

mistakes.pattern: Wrong verb form 'gaat' with ik: 'Ik gaat om elf uur naar de bibliotheek.'
mistakes.explain: With **ik**, gaan is 'ga': 'Ik ga om elf uur naar de bibliotheek.'

say.nl: En de bank? Is de bank vandaag open?
say.en: And the bank? Is the bank open today?

turns.task: Say that the bank is closed today, but open tomorrow.
examples: De bank is vandaag gesloten, maar morgen open.
De bank is vandaag dicht. Morgen is de bank open.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'op' with morgen: 'De bank is op morgen open.'
mistakes.explain: Do not use **op** with **morgen**: 'De bank is morgen open.'

mistakes.pattern: Wrong word order after 'maar morgen': 'De bank is vandaag dicht, maar morgen de bank is open.'
mistakes.explain: After **morgen**, the verb comes before the subject: 'maar morgen is de bank open.'

mistakes.pattern: Omits subject after 'maar': 'De bank is vandaag dicht, maar morgen is open.'
mistakes.explain: Add **de bank**: 'maar morgen is de bank open.'

mistakes.pattern: Says the bank is open today and closed tomorrow: 'De bank is vandaag open, maar morgen gesloten.'
mistakes.explain: The task says closed today and open tomorrow: 'De bank is vandaag gesloten, maar morgen open.'

culture.title: Openingstijden in Nederland
culture.text: Many shops in the Netherlands close around 18:00 on weekdays. One evening a week is often **koopavond**, usually Thursday or Friday, when shops stay open later. On Sundays many shops open later, often around 12:00, and close around 17:00 or 18:00. Opening hours differ by town and by shop, so check the **openingstijden** on the door or online.

summary: Name useful places in town: de bakker, de apotheek, de bibliotheek, het station.
Use naar for movement to a place, in for inside a place, and bij for at a shop or counter.
Ask Hoe laat gaat ... open/dicht? and answer with van ... tot ...
Gaan: ik ga, jij gaat, wij gaan; use naar before the place.
Open, dicht and gesloten are common on signs and in opening hours.
